result:
I've written `proposal.md` with 10 refactorings and a ranking. Nothing in `code/` was changed, and nothing was built or run, so the line counts are estimates.

Most of the evidence (file:line references, duplicate counts) comes from three read-only search agents. I re-checked a sample myself, and those all held up: the page-name literals in 8 files, the `getReportsList` entries and the duplicated private methods in `LandscapeReportGenerator` and `LandscapeReportContributorsTab`.

**Where the code has been changing:**
- **Report wiring:** `LandscapeReportGenerator` (130 commits), `ReportFileExporter` (94), `DataExporter` (68) and `SummaryUtils` (60).
- **Contributors and git history:** every change in the last 90 days, including the last commit on 2025‑09‑20.
- **File-level reports:** `FileSizeReportGenerator` and `FileChurnReportGenerator` keep changing together.
- **Language analyzers:** this is where most of the 1071 duplicate blocks are, but that code hasn't changed since 2022, so I didn't propose a big rewrite there.

**Ranked by expected benefit per line changed:**

| Rank | Id | Refactoring | Lines | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | R7 | Javadoc on about 15 entry-point classes naming the words people use and the other files that must change with them | ~120 | The code uses different words than a task would: churn vs "change frequency", landscape vs "across repositories". Comments only, so no risk. |
| 2 | R1 | One `ReportPages` list of each page's file name, title and icon | ~150 | Each page name is typed out in 6–11 places today. |
| 3 | R4 | One `ContributorIdentity` class for ignore, email-alias, person, team and bot rules | ~160 | This area is changing now, and one such change touches 6–7 files across two modules. |
| 4 | R2 | One `ReportDataFiles` list of export and visual file names | ~120 | 4–8 copies per name; the program that writes a file and the pages that link to it disagree silently if one side is renamed. |
| 5 | R5 | Named 30/90/180/365-day windows in one `ActivityWindows` class | ~150 | Three separate constants already mean "30 days", and the rest are bare numbers a search can't find. |
| 6 | R3 | Merge the ~300 copied contributor-chart lines between the two landscape classes | ~450, net −300 | Today an agent edits one copy and the other page stays wrong. Medium risk. |
| 7 | R6 | One shared renderer for the risk-distribution sections of the FileSize, FileChurn and FileAge reports | ~350, net −200 | 3–5 copies of each section, and these files change together. |
| 8 | R9 | Model-to-export mapping kept next to each export class, plus a test that fails when a field is missing | ~140 | Adding a field to an export currently means finding three files. |
| 9 | R8 | Command-line dispatch as one table, with named default paths | ~100 | Busy file (67 commits), but its changes are already mostly local. |
| 10 | R10 | One base class for the Julia, Lua and ObjectPascal unit extractors | ~250, net −150 | The largest duplicate blocks, but those files rarely change. |

The proposal also lists bugs we found while reading, which none of the refactorings may fix because they must keep behaviour identical. One example is that `ContributorRepositories.java:33` adds the 180-day commit count where it should add the 365-day one. One refactoring has to keep the misspelled output text in `FileSizeReportGenerator:164`, or the reports would change.

One thing outside the folder: I wrote a small helper script to `../g-design-tools/churn.sh` (one level above this folder). It never ran because permission was refused, so you can delete it.
